hypothesis: If an isotropic septal membrane under uniform pressure is a surface of minimal area, and is spherical when a straight cone is closed by a perpendicular planar attachment, then published measurements of real orthocone or straight-coned septa with that attachment will have essentially equal radii of curvature in two perpendicular sections.
pass_criterion: Pre-registered (claim supported). An admissible table (defined in test_contract) contains at least 10 real septa identified by the source as straight-coned or orthoconic with a planar, perpendicular attachment, each with a radius of curvature in a median section and a radius of curvature in a transverse section, both positive and finite. Supported if at least 80 percent of those septa have R_transverse / R_median inside [0.9, 1.1].
fail_criterion: Pre-registered (claim refuted). Refuted if at least 10 such septa are measured and fewer than 40 percent have the radius ratio inside [0.9, 1.1]. If the fraction is at least 40 percent and below 80 percent, the verdict is mixed. If no admissible table is retrieved, the verdict is inconclusive with reason data-unavailable. A surface that was generated as a minimal or minimum-curvature surface, a finite-element stress field, septal spacing angles, chamber volume, and a coiled Nautilus or Spirula septum are not admissible for this verdict.

test_contract.expected_observation: For at least 10 real straight-coned septa with a planar perpendicular suture, the transverse and median radii of curvature agree to within 10 percent on at least 80 percent of septa, which is the spherical cap Thompson states for that boundary.
test_contract.disconfirming_observation: Fewer than 40 percent of at least 10 such septa have the two radii within 10 percent, so the septum is not a spherical cap under the boundary condition for which the claim predicts a sphere.
test_contract.admissible_datasets: An openly downloadable numeric table, no login, of radii of curvature or mean curvature measured on real nautiloid, orthocone or ammonoid septa. The straight-cone spherical case requires the source to identify a straight cone and a planar perpendicular attachment. Surfaces constructed to be minimal, soap-film simulations, and 3D-printed theoretical septa are not measurements of organisms. Values read off a figure for this test are not admissible. A table whose numbers were already visible in a search snippet before this registration is not admissible for the verdict.
test_contract.inference_method: For each admissible septum, the ratio of the two published sectional radii. The verdict is the fraction of ratios inside [0.9, 1.1], with the thresholds in pass_criterion and fail_criterion. Mean curvature, if a table of H is found instead of two radii, is not substituted after the fact: the registered observable is the radius ratio. If that table is absent, the verdict is data-unavailable.

interpretation: Thompson equates an isotropic membrane under uniform pressure with a soap-bubble surface of minimal area, and then specialises the shape: a sphere for a straight circular cone closed perpendicularly, an ellipsoid for an oblique planar attachment, and a saddle for a sinuous attachment. This registration tests the spherical case, which is the one with a numerical signature (equal radii in perpendicular sections) that a published table can carry. A sphere has non-zero mean curvature, so it is not a minimal surface in the strict sense (H = 0); that distinction is not given a second verdict here, because no mean-curvature table was part of the registered observable. Nautilus is a coiled shell whose suture is not a single perpendicular plane; Thompson's own next paragraph treats its septal curvatures as unequal. A Nautilus radius is therefore outside the pass/fail rule.
caveats: Both assessors name MorphoSource micro-CT. Media download there requires a login, which this test does not use.

Before any septal measurement file was downloaded, landing pages and one data readme were read. Hoffmann et al. Dryad 10.5061/dryad.133nq (Zenodo record 5011159) documents conch diameters, expansion rates, septal spacing angles and chamber surface area and volume for one Kosmoceras, not two radii of curvature. Ikuno and colleagues' Dryad 10.5061/dryad.bzkh189gp is septal spacing as a rotational angle. Johnson et al. Dryad 10.5061/dryad.pvmcvdnk6 contains figures of 3D-printed theoretical septa. Lemanis 2020 constructs septal models as minimum-curvature surfaces, so those surfaces cannot test the claim. Lemanis 2016 (PeerJ, PMC5028744) publishes Nautilus and Spirula sectional radii; a web-search snippet showed that table before this registration, and the shells are coiled, so the table is excluded from the verdict and is not copied into measured.
No open table of orthocone septal radii meeting the contract was located in that search. If the script also finds none, the pre-registered verdict is inconclusive with reason data-unavailable.
